codeReview.summary: Fail with one blocking issue. The feature adds first-class `flux apps start|stop|restart|redeploy|redeploy-component` routing, keeps confirm-gated lifecycle mutations explicit, preserves the expected lifecycle flags, and surfaces parsed redeploy progress summaries from the persisted resource payloads. However, the semantic-progress reducer gives any final JSON `status: success` precedence over later plain-text events, so a mixed progress stream can still be reported as a successful redeploy even when the last parsed event is an error. That breaks the feature's requirement to return meaningful parsed progress/event summaries for VAL-APPS-005.

issues.description: `deriveProgressSemantic` returns success as soon as the last parsed JSON object has `status: success` (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:4971-4980`), before it considers whether later plain-text events report an error (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:4995-5005`). `parseProgressOutput` in MCP preserves later trailing text as ordered events (`flux-mcp/src/index.ts:374-404`), so a stream like `{"status":"success",...}` followed by `error: ...` will leave `lastEvent` as the error but still produce `semantic.ok === true`. Both `handleAppsRedeploy` and `handleAppsRedeployComponent` trust that semantic result for their top-level `ok`/`status` and exit code (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:6488-6514` and `6542-6568`), which means a failed redeploy can be surfaced as success instead of error. The new tests only cover pure-JSON success and pure-event failure, so this mixed-stream regression is not caught.
